title: Senior At-Home Care
desc: Plan and deliver safe, respectful at-home support for older adults: daily living, safety, medicines reminders, dignity and when to call for help.
outcomes: Explain the needs, rights and dignity of an older person at home.
Find fall, fire and medicine risks in a home.
Judge when a situation needs a professional or emergency help.
Build a written care routine and a family communication plan.
task: Produce a person-centred home care plan for a practice case, with a home safety check, daily routine, emergency card and carer wellbeing plan.
condition: A practice case or a consenting family, a phone, forms, two peers and a qualified nurse or care mentor. Nursing procedures are outside scope.
standard: Plan respects the person's wishes; safety check finds and fixes at least 8 risks; emergency card is complete; no clinical task is done outside training; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Family carers, home-care assistants, community volunteers, care entrepreneurs.
evidence: care plan, home safety checklist, routine, emergency card, carer plan

ladder: Respect and dignity

L1: learner can name basic needs of an older person. Focus module: Respect and dignity (Understand, 4 h). Care starts with the person, not the task. Key points: Ask what they want; offer choices; use their name. Protect privacy in washing, dressing and toilet care. Never treat an adult like a child.

Teach: open with the worked example. Mr Rao prefers tea at 7; the carer plans around it and keeps the bathroom door closed. Then set the activity: Write a "what matters to me" page with the person. Mark against the standard: Page uses their words. Check at this level: Why use their words? Model answer: It keeps dignity and choice. Start with respect.
Home safety check

L2: learner knows dignity and safety rules. Focus module: Home safety check (Analyse, 5 h). Most harm at home is preventable. Key points: Falls: loose rugs, poor light, wet floors, no rails. Fire and electrical hazards; gas safety. Easy-to-reach items and clear paths.

Teach: open with the worked example. A carer removes a loose mat and fits a night light, ending night-time stumbles. Then set the activity: Complete a checklist for one home. Mark against the standard: At least 8 risks found, each with a fix and date. Check at this level: Name three fall risks. Model answer: Loose rugs, poor light, wet floors. Show safety signs.
Daily living support

L3: learner can complete a home safety check. Focus module: Daily living support (Apply, 5 h). Support independence, not dependence. Key points: Meals, drinks and nutrition; assist with mobility; hygiene. Do with, not for, whenever possible. Safe lifting: ask for training; use aids.

Teach: open with the worked example. The carer sets out clothes in order and lets Mrs Iyer dress herself. Then set the activity: Plan a day routine with times. Mark against the standard: Routine covers meals, fluids, movement, rest and social time. Check at this level: Who decides doses? Model answer: The prescriber. Practise a check.
Medicines and health reminders

L4: learner can deliver a daily routine. Focus module: Medicines and health reminders (Apply, 4 h). Carers remind; clinicians decide. Key points: Use a pill organiser prepared by a pharmacist or nurse. Record what was taken; never change doses. Report new symptoms promptly.

Teach: open with the worked example. A weekly box with morning and evening slots reduces missed doses. Then set the activity: Create a reminder chart and record sheet. Mark against the standard: Chart matches the prescriber's list. Check at this level: When call emergency? Model answer: Chest pain, stroke signs, serious fall, breathing trouble. Role-play.
Mind, mood and memory

L5: learner can handle medicines reminders and emergencies. Focus module: Mind, mood and memory (Apply, 4 h). Loneliness and forgetfulness are common. Key points: Keep routine; use calendars and clocks; encourage activity. Be patient; do not argue about facts when kind redirection works. Watch for sudden confusion, which can mean illness.

Teach: open with the worked example. A daily 15-minute walk and a call to a grandchild lifts mood. Then set the activity: Plan a weekly social schedule. Mark against the standard: Includes five activities. Check at this level: What is "do with, not for"? Model answer: Support independence by helping only as needed. Emergency drills.
Family and carer wellbeing

L6: learner can coordinate a team. Focus module: Family and carer wellbeing (Evaluate, 3 h). Carers burn out. Key points: Share the load; take breaks; ask for respite. Keep a shared log or group message. Seek local support groups.

Teach: open with the worked example. Siblings take alternate weekends; stress drops. Then set the activity: Write a carer plan. Mark against the standard: Plan names who, when, what. Check at this level: Name one mood tip. Model answer: Daily activity and social contact. Cover rota.
Review and improve

L7: learner can audit a care plan. Focus module: Review and improve (Create, 4 h). Care plans change as needs change. Key points: Review monthly or after any event. Track weight, sleep, mood, falls. Celebrate good days.

Teach: open with the worked example. After a fall, a rail and a physiotherapy visit are added. Then set the activity: Present your plan review. Mark against the standard: Changes are dated and agreed with the person. Check at this level: What is sudden confusion a sign of? Model answer: Possible illness; seek help. Peer audit.
